# Qwen3-Embedding

## 1 Introduction

The Qwen3 Embedding model series is the latest proprietary model of the Qwen family, specifically designed for text embedding and ranking tasks. Building upon the dense foundational models of the Qwen3 series, it provides a comprehensive range of text embeddings and reranking models in various sizes (0.6B, 4B, and 8B). This guide describes how to run the model with vLLM Ascend. Note that only vLLM Ascend 0.9.2rc1 and higher versions support the model.

## 2 Supported Features

Refer to Supported Features List to get the model's supported feature matrix.

## 3 Prerequisites

### 3.1 Model Weight

Weight Version  | Download Links
--- | ---
`Qwen3-Embedding-8B`  | ModelScope
`Qwen3-Embedding-4B`  | ModelScope
`Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`  | ModelScope

It is recommended to download the model weight to the shared directory of multiple nodes, such as `/root/.cache/`.

> Path description: Download the model weights to a directory of your choice and record it. ## 5 Online Service Deployment {: #5-online-service-deployment }

=== "Ascend 950DT&950PR Products/A3/A2"
    
    ````shell
    vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B \
      --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B \
      --runner pooling \
      --port 8000 \
      --max-model-len 1024
    ```
    `

=== "Atlas 300I DUO"
    
    ````shell
    #!/bin/sh
    # Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download
    vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B  \
      --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B  \
      --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1024,512]}' \
      --additional-config '{"ascend_compilation_config": {"fuse_norm_quant": false}}' \
      --runner pooling \
      --dtype float16 \
      --port 8000 \
      --max-model-len 1024
    ```
    Required  Parameter Descriptions:
    
    `--compilation-config` For Atlas 300I DUO, due to limited hardware streams, the size of cudagraph_capture_sizes is restricted.
    `

Key Parameter Descriptions:

  * `--max-model-len` represents the context length, which is the maximum value of the input plus output for a single request. For Atlas 300I DUO if automatic parsing resolves to a large context length, allocating this mask (O(max_model_len^2)) may exceed NPU memory and trigger OOM. Be sure to set an explicit and conservative value, such as --max-model-len 1024.

Common Issues Tip: If you encounter issues, please refer to the Public FAQs for troubleshooting.

## 6 Functional Verification

Once your server is started, you can verify by follow command:

Service Verification:
    
    curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/embeddings -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
      "input": [
            "The capital of China is Beijing.",
            "Gravity is a force that attracts two bodies towards each other. It gives weight to physical objects and is responsible for the movement of planets around the sun."
        ]
    }'

## 7 Accuracy Evaluation

Here are two accuracy evaluation methods.

### 7.1 Using MTEB

  1. Refer to MTEB for details.

  2. Run follow code to execute the accuracy evaluation.
    
    import os
    import mteb
    
    from mteb.models.vllm_wrapper import VllmEncoderWrapper
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
    
        data_path = "/home/data/mteb_data"
        os.environ["HF_DATASETS_CACHE"] = data_path
        os.environ["HF_ENDPOINT"] = "https://hf-mirror.com"
    
        model = VllmEncoderWrapper(f"/root/.cache/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B",
                                    revision="norm",
                                    dtype="float16",
                                    max_model_len=10240,
                                   )
    
        cache = mteb.ResultCache("/home/data/mteb_data")
        tasks = mteb.get_tasks(tasks=["LeCaRDv2"])
        results = mteb.evaluate(model, tasks=tasks, cache=cache, encode_kwargs={"batch_size": 2}, overwrite_strategy="always")
        df = results.to_dataframe()
        print(df)

  3. After execution, you can get the result.

## 8 Performance Evaluation

### 8.1 Using vLLM Benchmark

Run performance of `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` as an example. Refer to vllm benchmark for more details.

Take the `serve` as an example. Run the code as follows.
    
    vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B --backend openai-embeddings --port 8000 --dataset-name random --endpoint /v1/embeddings --random-input 200 --save-result --result-dir ./

After about several minutes, you can get the performance evaluation result.

## v0.30.0 - 2026.10.29

This is the stable release of vLLM Ascend v0.30.0, built on the v0.29 release line and aligned with upstream vLLM v0.30.0 via the main2main pipeline. Building on v0.30.0rc1, this release integrates FlashMLA decode with DCP and DSpark, extends KV Pool layerwise pooling and PCP speculative decoding, hardens EPLB for the new quantization formats, and fixes the stability issues across attention, MoE, KV transfer, and Model Runner V2 execution reported during the RC cycle. It still focuses on the flagship models: DeepSeek V4.1, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8-27B, DeepSeek V4-Flash/Pro, Kimi K3. Model or hardware combinations outside the scope declared in v0.30.0 are not part of the release claims. Please follow the official documentation to get started.

PR references marked with † were merged into the v0.30.0 release branch before v0.30.0rc1.

> Notice: In this version, modelrunner still defaults to v1, but some models require v2 to be enabled for support. For specific information, please refer to the model tutorial. We plan to fully switch to Model Runner V2 in the next version.

### Highlights

  * DeepSeek V4.1: Added DeepSeek V4.1 support on Model Runner V2, enabled torch.compile, and sped up startup via in-place rotary embedding, reused filtered RoPE lookups, and removed redundant DSV4.1 indexer/SP copies; added the TurboQuant 4-bit latent KV cache for DSA sparse models (DeepSeek V4 Flash; A2/A3 only), including packed KV cache in the V1 runner; fixed ModelSlim-quantized DSV4 weight layout and added AscendStore preparation for V4.1, and packaged attention operators (QLI/QSLI/MQSMLA) with DSL.   * Qwen3.8-27B: Supported non-contiguous KV cache in hybrid linear-attention models, respected per-layer KV cache dtype and kept KV cache contiguous for paged attention, restored C8 V scales on hybrid cache page reassignment, restored Mamba block tables before deferred PP postprocessing, added the FLA NPU backend for GDN prefill, and fixed 310P performance and kernel compatibility for quantized deployment. #14340 #17924 #18003 #17956 #17954 #17565 #17534 #16420 #17964 #17278†
  * Kimi K3 on Ascend: Added end-to-end Kimi K3 support, including MLA DSpark speculative decoding, no-RoPE MLAPO on Ascend 950, fused QKV projections, fused norm gate and attention residual, EPLB, MegaMoE, and projector rotation. #12950 #13277 #13507 #13989 #13509 #14231†
  * GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 / DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 accuracy and performance: Resolved GLM-5.2 DSpark acceptance regressions and DeepSeek V4 Flash-0731 / Pro-0813 accuracy issues (reasoning-effort alignment, routed SwiGLU limit, and frontend behavior), and reused DSV4 compressor metadata across layers for better performance. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
